messages.subject: Re: Downloading package dynamically
messages.body_plain:
Hi Rodrigo,
What you need is aether-package-loader, which will download packages as required.
https://github.com/bedatadriven/renjin/tree/master/tools/aether-package-loader

This an implementation of the PackageLoader interface that will load packages dynamically, using the Eclipse Aether library <http://www.eclipse.org/aether/> in the background.

You will need to use SessionBuilder to create a new Session with this PackageLoader:

   Session session = new SessionBuilder()
    .bind(PackageLoader.class, new AetherPackageLoader())
    .build();

   RenjinScriptEngine engine = RenjinScriptEngineFactory.getScriptEngine(session);

What kind of build tool are you using? Or rather how are you managing your dependencies? You can of course manually download the individual jars from our Nexus repository <https://nexus.bedatadriven.com/content/groups/public/org/renjin/renjin-aether-package-loader/>, but you will need to also chase down all the transitive aether dependencies, which would be kind of pain.

If you are managing dependencies by hand, the quickest fix might be to use Ivy, which you could just use for resolving and
downloading the jars into a directory for your project.

<ivy-module version="2.0">
    <info organisation="org.apache" module="hello-ivy"/>
    <dependencies>
        <dependency org="org.renjin" name="renjin-script-engine" rev="0.7.1578"/>
        <dependency org="org.renjin" name="renjin-aether-package-loader" rev="0.7.1578"/>
    </dependencies>
</ivy-module>

HTH,
Alex

Thanks again.....

Rodrigo

Hi,

I've been working for some time with Renjin on a number of Java projects using both Maven and Gradle to manage the Renjin lib dependencies and everything works smoothly. However I've recently begun a Scala project which uses the Scala build tool (sbt) to manage lib dependencies. For reasons as yet unknown when I declare a managed dependency on Renjin in build.sbt that dependency can not be resolved. The error I'm seeing on the build is as follows:

[warn] ==== BeDataDriven: tried
[warn]   http://nexus.bedatadriven.com/content/groups/public/org/renjin/renjin-script-engine/0.8.1890/renjin-script-engine-0.8.1890.pom
[info] Resolving org.fusesource.jansi#jansi;1.4 ...
[warn]  ::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::

[warn]  ::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::
[warn]  :: org.renjin#renjin-script-engine;0.8.1890: not found
[warn]  ::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::
[warn]
[warn]  Note: Unresolved dependencies path:
[warn]    org.renjin:renjin-script-engine:0.8.1890 (/Users/david/Desktop/delete-me/renjin-test/build.

The complete output generated by the sbt build failure can be found in the build-fail.txt file attached.

A minimal build.sbt that can be used to reproduce this problem looks as follows:

resolvers +=
  "BeDataDriven" at "http://nexus.bedatadriven.com/content/groups/public"

lazy val root = (project in file(".")).
  settings(
    name := "renjin-test",
    version := "1.0",
    scalaVersion := "2.10.6",
    libraryDependencies += "org.renjin" % "renjin-script-engine" % "0.8.1890"
  )

The resolver points at the BeDataDriven repo. In this case the dependency identifies the latest Renjin 0.8.x build although the problem is not unique to this version, it happens for all versions.

For the record, I'm using SBT 0.13 and Scala 2.10. Any help you can provide to get me past this hurdle is much appreciated.

Thanks,
David

messages.body_plain:
Hi Rodrigo,
I believe this should only be a warning - unfortunately the C/Fortran code for deSolve failed to compile under GCC bridge:
http://packages.renjin.org/package/org.renjin.cran/deSolve/1.12/build/36

which means that the java class org.renjin.cran.deSolve.deSolve, which would normally hold the compiled C/Fortran methods is not available.

I took a look at this particular failure and it seems linked to the way we're handling record types in GCC-Bridge, which is going to require some additional work in the very short term. I've opened a bug report here to keep track of it:
https://github.com/bedatadriven/renjin/issues/141

In the meantime, this means that any functions in deSolve that rely on the C/Fortran code will fail, though if there are any R functions that don't rely on native code, they should be able to run.

Alex

messages.subject: Re: Bug in RenjingScriptEngineFactory?
messages.body_plain:
Hi Rodrigo,
The SessionBuilder gives you more control about a whole host of things, including which packages are loaded on startup. If you want the same behavior as the RenjinScriptEngineFactory, then I think you can call "withDefaultPackages" which will load the expected default packages on startup, including stats, in which fivenum is defined.

I'm guessing the JRuby syntax looks something like:

session = SessionBuilder.new
.bind(PackageLoader.java_class, AetherPackageLoader.new)
.withDefaultPackages
.build

You could also change your R code to:

sap = R.sapply(i39, "stats::fivenum")

And it should work as well.

Best,
Alex
